correctness.rationale: Conditional on the established exact one-dimensional p-band theorem, the finite product iterate F^(dp) is explicitly a product of exact scalar returns on every phase cell, hence exact by tensor approximation. The affine phase shift is derived from the map, including k=0 and k=dp in the fixed-point count. Index-cycle telescoping gives p^g fixed points exactly when p divides k/g; Burnside and Möbius inversion complete the ergodic-component spectrum. The finite verifier exhausts 18 d,p cases and 230 fixed-count tests and checks the beta=11/10 band intervals as reduced rationals. Infinite quantifiers follow from the written derivation, not the checks. Scope is relative to the invariant ac product measure only.

originality.rationale: The focal article supplies the family and its known scalar periodic windows, and the 1991 reference treats scalar band return systems; neither inspected text supplies the exact affine-carry spectrum for all delayed product dimensions. The 1994 text discusses a different synchronous diffusively coupled product, which motivates comparisons but does not imply the delayed shift-with-carry sector census as written. The numerical 16-region example alone does not constitute a proven count of ergodic phase cycles. The proposal is only the model-specific exhaustive all-d delayed classification. Finite-group counting ingredients are classical, with historical priority uncertainty stated below.
residual_risks: Classical finite affine-permutation orbit formulas may have been published under shift-register or wreath-product terminology, without model-specific delayed-tent phrasing.
An unindexed historical derivation may specialize earlier general theory to exactly the same zero-coupling delay system; the negative targeted searches alone cannot exclude this.
The claim is strictly for the exact zero-coupling invariant core; it must not be conflated with the source's nonzero-coupling period phase diagram or with a global real-plane statement.

value.rationale: The motivating article displays phase cycling in a two-dimensional delayed map and points to higher delay dimensions; the precise number and least lengths of stationary density cycles are natural missing invariants. This theorem provides the exact complete all-d histogram, including nontrivial mixed-period components for d=3,p=4, and explains why 16 visible phase regions at beta=11/10 should not be interpreted as one 16-step ergodic cycle. These are structural distinctions in the dynamics of densities, beyond correctness of a simple band count, with a direct reusable formula.
